slot.brief: Gaseous AB-type dissociation set up as an ICE table; from total equilibrium pressure find degree of dissociation and then Kp.

stem: Initially, a vessel contains only $\text{AB(g)}$ at $0.8$ atm. At constant temperature and volume, it dissociates as $\text{AB(g)} \rightleftharpoons \text{A(g)}+\text{B(g)}$. If the total equilibrium pressure is $1.2$ atm, what is $K_p$?

verdicts.working: At constant temperature and volume, let the pressure change from dissociation be x. Then total pressure is 0.8 + x = 1.2, so x = 0.4 atm. Thus p_AB = p_A = p_B = 0.4 atm, and K_p = p_A p_B/p_AB = 0.4 atm.

working:
$P_{\text{tot}}=P_0(1+\alpha)\Rightarrow\alpha=\dfrac{1.2}{0.8}-1=0.5$
$p_{\text{AB}}=0.8(1-0.5)=0.4\,\text{atm};\quad p_{\text{A}}=p_{\text{B}}=0.8(0.5)=0.4\,\text{atm}$
$K_p=\dfrac{p_{\text{A}}p_{\text{B}}}{p_{\text{AB}}}=\dfrac{0.4\times0.4}{0.4}=0.4\,\text{atm}$

Independent check: At constant temperature and volume, let the pressure change from dissociation be x. Then total pressure is 0.8 + x = 1.2, so x = 0.4 atm. Thus p_AB = p_A = p_B = 0.4 atm, and K_p = p_A p_B/p_AB = 0.4 atm.
solution:
For degree of dissociation $\alpha$, $P_{\text{tot}}=P_0(1+\alpha)$, so $\alpha=\frac{1.2}{0.8}-1=0.5$. Thus $p_{\text{AB}}=0.4$ atm and $p_{\text{A}}=p_{\text{B}}=0.4$ atm.
$$K_p=\frac{p_{\text{A}}p_{\text{B}}}{p_{\text{AB}}}=\frac{0.4\times0.4}{0.4}=0.4\text{ atm}$$
